title: Dejan at the Japanese Tea Garden, and a reading player
summary: Dejan says he was hired at the Japanese Tea Garden despite weak reading and tells of a rival band playing next door, with a player who could only read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: You know, that's what I said. Well, that's why they hired me at the Japanese T-Guard. Because I was just not clear. I'd hold a note, see, when they finished playing, I'd hold a note. Do it, then it's not the right key, you know. Couldn't make no jazz. I didn't know if I could read that. Yeah. That's right. But I tell you, in them days, it helped so much. Now you take this fella, like Hickman, he could play a little saxophone, but he couldn't read so much, you see. And we was playing next door to one another. And I'll tell you the truth, at 11 o'clock at night, they packed up, getting at the Model T-4, and going on, Model T-4 ain't even fixing the move yet. See, everybody was over at our place. Seven o'clock in the morning, Mr. Baradice said, look, why don't y'all go to sleep a little while. Call up your mother, son. He said, I'm going to some of my friends, and we have a little port-a-pay on another night's awake. And we said, are you all right? He said, I'll call up my mother, tell her I'm still out here. And he'd be back about eight o'clock with some of his friends, we played until about 10, 11 o'clock, and they're dead. Another place closed, flattened. We'd go home to sleep, come back that night, same thing. We'd go home every night, 11 o'clock, until Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. It's only night he said, I'm talking about one, two o'clock in the morning. That's right. And me, I'm just playing that straight melody, holding that door on the air. That fellow, he always could read.

Hold that door on the air. Always could read. That's all he could do, read. That fellow, boy, that fellow. Always could read. You buy that piece of music, that was it. That was it. Always could read. In the never band, you played baritone.
Baritone, tenor, alto, tenor. Yeah, yeah. Never band. I didn't buy none of them.
